implementation.name: original-v1-systolic-array
implementation.scope: Declared weight-stationary 2×2 slice inside the original schematic: row inputs 2 and 3, every PE weight 1, two-term column reductions. Horizontal values and vertical partial sums advance on explicit skewed clocks. Other source FIFOs/accumulators illustrate the surrounding array and are outside this slice. No full-array utilization or DRAM-saving model.
implementation.question: How does a skewed wavefront reuse neighboring values?

purpose: How does a value get reused by its neighbor?

storyboard.label: Stage skewed row inputs
storyboard.description: The two-row, two-column slice starts with all PE weights fixed at 1 and column sums zero. Row input 2 enters first; row input 3 is delayed one clock so its reduction index meets the partial sum from above.

storyboard.label: Clock 1: upper-left MAC
storyboard.description: The upper-left PE consumes 2 and its local weight 1. It retains sum 2 for the next row and forwards input 2 toward the right neighbor.

storyboard.label: Clock 2: advance one wavefront
storyboard.description: Upper-right reuses input 2 and produces sum 2. Concurrently lower-left consumes input 3 and upper-left’s sum 2, producing 5. Each input meets the matching partial sum.

storyboard.label: Clock 3: finish lower-right
storyboard.description: Lower-right consumes input 3 and upper-right’s sum 2, producing 5. Column 1’s completed 5 drains to its bottom accumulator.

storyboard.label: Drain the remaining completed column
storyboard.description: Column 2’s completed 5 drains into its bottom accumulator. The result was not emitted while either reduction contribution was missing.

guard: Clock-skewed weight-stationary two-row two-column slice; partial sums retained to matching reduction arrival; no premature output, no DRAM or throughput multiplier.
